- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior peak.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and prices are falling, model often underestimates the drop; adjust downward by 1–3% to match recent trend.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior high), model frequently overshoots in next period; cap forecast at 1–2% below prior peak.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish within 3–5 days, model often fails to adjust; apply mean reversion to 10–15 day moving average.
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently overestimates near the end of the horizon; reduce final 3–5 days by 1–3% to reflect diminishing momentum.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.34–0.67) and history shows volatility, model tends to smooth too much; allow 1–2% volatility buffer in forecast range.
